description: Real-time data pipeline from Wear OS watch to phone companion app: watch collects HR, HRV, SpO2 and stress index, transmits via MessageClient, phone displays live readings in StatusScreen and relays each reading to the Node+Postgres backend.

userStories.title: Add play-services-wearable to phone module
userStories.description: As a developer, I need play-services-wearable in the :app module so the phone can participate in the Wearable Data Layer and receive messages from the watch.
acceptanceCriteria: gradle/libs.versions.toml already has playServicesWearable = "18.0.0" under [versions] and play-services-wearable under [libraries] — verify it is present, add if missing
app/build.gradle.kts implementation dependencies include libs.play.services.wearable
wear/build.gradle.kts implementation dependencies also include libs.play.services.wearable (verify, add if missing)
./gradlew :app:assembleDebug completes without error
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: play-services-wearable is already declared in libs.versions.toml at version 18.0.0. Only the :app build.gradle.kts dependency line is likely missing. Verify :wear has it too.

userStories.title: Add Retrofit and Gson to phone module
userStories.description: As a developer, I need Retrofit and converter-gson in the :app module so the phone can POST sensor readings to the Node+Postgres backend.
acceptanceCriteria: app/build.gradle.kts implementation dependencies include libs.retrofit2 and libs.retrofit2.converter.gson
libs.retrofit2 and libs.retrofit2.converter.gson are already in libs.versions.toml — verify, add if missing
./gradlew :app:assembleDebug completes without error
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: retrofit2 and retrofit2-converter-gson are already declared in libs.versions.toml. Only the :app build.gradle.kts dependency lines are missing. Mirror the pattern from wear/build.gradle.kts.

userStories.title: Define SensorBundle data model and MessagePaths in both modules
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a consistent data structure and message path constants in both modules so the watch sender and phone receiver speak the same JSON protocol.
acceptanceCriteria: wear/src/main/java/com/pl/pulselab/model/SensorBundle.kt created with data class SensorBundle(val bpm: Int, val hrv: Int, val spo2: Int, val stressIndex: Int, val timestamp: Long)
wear/src/main/java/com/pl/pulselab/model/MessagePaths.kt created with object MessagePaths { const val SENSOR_DATA = "/sensor/data" }
app/src/main/java/com/pl/pulselab/model/SensorBundle.kt created with identical fields
app/src/main/java/com/pl/pulselab/model/MessagePaths.kt created with identical constant
./gradlew :wear:assembleDebug and ./gradlew :app:assembleDebug both complete without error
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: No shared Gradle module — each module owns its own copy. JSON is the contract. Gson is available transitively via converter-gson in both modules once US-002 is done.

userStories.title: Extend wear data model and simulation to all 4 metrics
userStories.description: As a developer, I need HeartRateRepository to produce HRV, SpO2 and stress index alongside BPM so a complete SensorBundle can be assembled on every tick.
acceptanceCriteria: wear/src/main/java/com/pl/pulselab/model/HeartRateReading.kt updated to include hrv: Int, spo2: Int, stressIndex: Int fields alongside existing bpm
Simulation mode in HeartRateRepository generates plausible values: HRV 30–80 ms, SpO2 95–100, stress 0–100 (use Random.nextInt with appropriate ranges)
HomeViewModel state carries all 4 values (update HomeUiState.Monitoring or equivalent sealed class variant)
HomeScreen.kt compiles and does not crash after the model extension (update any when-exhaustive branches)
./gradlew :wear:assembleDebug completes without error
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Depends on US-003. Only touches the :wear module. Keep the SIMULATE constant pattern in HeartRateRepository — just extend the emitted values. The HomeScreen UI does not need to display the new fields yet, just must not crash.

userStories.title: Send SensorBundle from watch to phone via MessageClient
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the watch to transmit each sensor reading to the phone in real time so the phone can display and relay it.
acceptanceCriteria: wear/src/main/java/com/pl/pulselab/data/wearable/WearDataSender.kt created as a plain class with a suspend fun send(context: Context, bundle: SensorBundle) method

send() discovers connected nodes via Wearable.getNodeClient(context).connectedNodes.await() and sends to each node via Wearable.getMessageClient(context).sendMessage(nodeId, MessagePaths.SENSOR_DATA, gson.toJson(bundle).toByteArray()).await()
send() is wrapped in try/catch — any exception is caught and logged with Log.e(); no exception propagates to the caller
HomeViewModel calls WearDataSender.send() on each new reading inside the existing collection coroutine
Any existing direct ApiRepository calls for posting to the backend in HomeViewModel are removed or commented out with a // migrated to phone relay note
./gradlew :wear:assembleDebug completes without error
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Depends on US-003 and US-004. Use kotlinx-coroutines-play-services Task.await() extension — add to wear/build.gradle.kts if not already present (artifact: org.jetbrains.kotlinx:kotlinx-coroutines-play-services, same version as kotlinxCoroutines in libs.versions.toml). Context is passed in from the ViewModel via the Application context.

userStories.title: Create WearableListenerService on phone
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a background service on the phone that receives MessageClient messages from the watch and makes them available to the UI layer via a singleton state holder.
acceptanceCriteria: app/src/main/java/com/pl/pulselab/data/wearable/SensorDataStore.kt created as a Kotlin object with val sensorFlow: MutableStateFlow<SensorBundle?> = MutableStateFlow(null)
app/src/main/java/com/pl/pulselab/data/wearable/WearListenerService.kt created extending WearableListenerService
onMessageReceived() checks that event.path == MessagePaths.SENSOR_DATA, decodes event.data via Gson into SensorBundle, then emits to SensorDataStore.sensorFlow
WearListenerService uses a CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob() + Dispatchers.IO); scope is cancelled in onDestroy()
app/AndroidManifest.xml declares the service with android:exported="false" and an intent-filter with action com.google.android.gms.wearable.MESSAGE_RECEIVED
./gradlew :app:assembleDebug completes without error
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Depends on US-003. SensorDataStore as a Kotlin object is the standard bridge between Service lifecycle and ViewModel lifecycle. The Wearable runtime starts WearListenerService automatically — do not start it manually or in Application.onCreate().

userStories.title: Create phone-side ApiService and ApiRepository for backend relay
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a network layer in the :app module so the phone can POST each received SensorBundle to the Node+Postgres backend.
acceptanceCriteria: app/src/main/java/com/pl/pulselab/data/network/ApiService.kt created with a Retrofit interface defining @POST("readings") suspend fun postReading(@Body bundle: SensorBundle): Response<Unit>

app/src/main/java/com/pl/pulselab/data/network/ApiRepository.kt created with const val BASE_URL = "https://TODO.replace.me/" and an OkHttpClient with an Authorization header interceptor (token as const val API_TOKEN = "TODO")
ApiRepository exposes suspend fun postReading(bundle: SensorBundle): Result<Unit> that wraps the Retrofit call in runCatching
./gradlew :app:assembleDebug completes without error
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Depends on US-002 and US-003. Mirror the pattern from wear/src/main/java/com/pl/pulselab/data/network/. BASE_URL and API_TOKEN are intentional TODOs — do not invent values. Use Response<Unit> (not Call<Unit>) since this is a suspend function.

userStories.title: Create StatusViewModel connected to live sensor data and backend relay
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a ViewModel that collects from SensorDataStore, posts each reading to the backend, and exposes a state object for StatusScreen to render.
acceptanceCriteria: app/src/main/java/com/pl/pulselab/presentation/status/StatusViewModel.kt created extending AndroidViewModel (needs Application for context)
StatusViewModel collects SensorDataStore.sensorFlow; on each non-null bundle it calls apiRepository.postReading(bundle) on Dispatchers.IO
StatusViewModel exposes statusUiState: StateFlow<StatusUiState> where StatusUiState is a data class with fields: bundle: SensorBundle?, isSyncing: Boolean, lastSyncTime: String?, syncError: String?
On successful POST: isSyncing = false, lastSyncTime = formatted current time (HH:mm), syncError = null
On failed POST: isSyncing = false, syncError = exception message or "Erro de conexão", lastSyncTime unchanged
./gradlew :app:assembleDebug completes without error
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Depends on US-006 and US-007. Use viewModelScope for coroutines. Format lastSyncTime with java.time.LocalTime.now() and DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("HH:mm") — available at minSdk 30+. StatusUiState should be a plain data class, not a sealed class.

userStories.title: Refactor StatusScreen to stateless/stateful split and wire to StatusViewModel
userStories.description: As a researcher using the phone app, I want StatusScreen to display live sensor readings and real sync status from the watch instead of hardcoded values.
acceptanceCriteria: StatusScreen.kt refactored into: StatusScreen(viewModel: StatusViewModel) stateful wrapper that collects statusUiState and calls StatusScreenContent; and StatusScreenContent(uiState: StatusUiState) stateless composable — following the same pattern as HomeScreen.kt in the wear module
All 4 metric cards (HR, HRV, SpO2, stress) show values from uiState.bundle; when bundle is null each value displays "--"
"Estado do Servidor" row shows "Online" in green on last successful POST, "Erro" in red when syncError is non-null
"Sincronização" row shows spinning Sync icon while isSyncing = true; shows "Concluído" when lastSyncTime is set; shows "Falhou" when syncError is non-null
"Último Envio" row shows lastSyncTime value (e.g. "Hoje às 14:32") or "--" when null
MainActivity.kt updated to instantiate StatusViewModel via viewModel() and pass it to StatusScreen(viewModel)
./gradlew :app:assembleDebug completes without error
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Depends on US-008. Import androidx.lifecycle.viewmodel.compose:lifecycle-viewmodel-compose for the viewModel() composable — already in libs.versions.toml as lifecycleViewmodelCompose. StatusScreenContent keeps the existing hardcoded color palette (Navy, Teal, etc.) — only the data values change.
